findings: The November capture is a complete Connect implementation guide, with a private-preview email request route. Waitlist submission is an access request and precedes any grant, merchant/location setup or payment (new raw lines 9-23,38-42). The May capture already stated private preview (old raw lines 8-10); the new access instructions add a route and do not establish GA.

The May guide passed the already-provisioned establishment's SIRET on direct and platform PaymentIntents (old raw lines 25-50,112-128,145-160). The November Connect guide requires preview Stripe version 2026-05-27.preview or later and moves to a merchant-of-record PaymentLocation and capability request, then passes the location and `if_payment_method_is_eligible` (new raw lines 38-59,130-147,165-185). The separate November payment guide says Stripe resolves the SIRET at confirmation and that updates do not change already-confirmed payments (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md:58-74`). The November product overview still tells readers to pass a pre-provisioned SIRET (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-2026-11-07.md:119-129`). Add reciprocal scope on the concept (lines 33–38,49–60,74–87) and related acceptance, overview and setup routes. The November Dashboard onboarding guide is a separate UI path and explicitly shows the Payment Location ID after onboarding (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-2026-11-07.md:25-35,38-56`), so the API route does not by itself retire Dashboard onboarding.

The May Connect sample and current source line 31 use a scalar on PaymentMethod (old raw lines 58-72). November Connect shows an array for `PaymentMethod.card.benefits.programs` but still shows a scalar for `ConfirmationToken.payment_method_preview.card.benefits.programs` (new raw lines 74-109). Even the separate November product overview shows a scalar for PaymentMethod (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-2026-11-07.md:131-148`). Warn the mapped source and reciprocal voucher concept (line 59) about the object-specific examples and conflicting PaymentMethod shapes. The snapshots do not establish a universal schema or a general API migration from scalar to array.

The separate November setup API mentions destination charges with `on_behalf_of` as a merchant-of-record example for provisioning (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:312-340`). The Connect payment support matrix explicitly rules out destination and separate charges and transfers (new raw lines 25-36). Its Before/After headings illustrate moving away from those patterns. The destination Before prose says `transfer_data[destination]` but the example only shows `on_behalf_of`, so don't treat it as a complete destination-charge template. The platform After examples keep `on_behalf_of` while omitting voucher proceeds transfers and the prohibited PaymentIntent fields (new raw lines 112-183). Add reciprocal scope to the related setup and Connect concept routes.

The mapped source's fee rule (line 34) omits the linked Account Debits requirements and belongs to the platform-charge flow. In the November guide Stripe deducts its processing fees from the platform, the post-capture application fee uses a transfer on the connected account to the platform, and the issuer settles voucher proceeds directly with the connected account (new raw lines 62-68,187-218,220-235). The separate Account Debits guide qualifies the fee transfer by platform negative-balance responsibility, binding consent, default currency, balance conditions, and supported regions/corridors (`raw/stripe-connect-account-debits-2026-11-07.md:15-56`). A fee transfer reversal returns the application fee and leaves the no-voucher-refund rule intact.

The related November API setup guide states a per-location `fr_meal_vouchers_conecs_payments` capability, a `pending` request and `active` as the acceptance gate, even if supported issuers arrive earlier (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:96-112,137-172,192-198`). It requires CNTR licensing and issuer contracts for the requested issuers and describes Connected Account scoping if it is merchant of record (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:5-13,312-340`). Location creation or eligibility detection provides no proof of an active capability or paid transaction.
substantive_changes: New preview version floor and merchant-of-record PaymentLocation plus capability route replace the old SIRET provisioning instruction for this Connect API flow (old raw lines 25-27, new raw lines 38-42).

The connected-account direct charge and platform charge conversion examples use location ID and conditional voucher enablement in place of a literal SIRET. Reference the confirmation-time resolution route (old raw lines 31-50,112-160 and new raw lines 46-68,130-185).

The PaymentMethod example changes scalar to array without a matching ConfirmationToken change (old raw lines 58-92 and new raw lines 74-109). The preview waitlist gains an explicit contact/request path (old raw lines 8-10 and new raw lines 9-23). Table padding, Node-to-cURL fee and reversal examples, and the added text diagram do not change the charge-type support matrix or fee/settlement direction.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve May 5, 2026 evidence for direct SIRET provisioning on the merchant of record and raw SIRET request field. Keep November's overview wording separately qualified instead of assuming a product-wide retirement of that field (old raw lines 1-2,25-50,112-160).

Both guides retain platform and direct charges and rule out destination and separate charges and transfers because voucher proceeds settle outside Stripe (old raw lines 12-23,215-218; new raw lines 25-36,232-235).

SetupIntent setup saves without charging and returns a PaymentMethod inspected after the save. Payment Element integration instead inspects a ConfirmationToken preview before server PaymentIntent creation. Preserve classification versus successful payment and the dated sample shape differences (old raw lines 54-92 and new raw lines 70-109).

Retain the platform flow's post-capture application fee debit and optional fee reversal separately from issuer settlement and voucher refund limitations (old raw lines 163-218 and new raw lines 187-235).

The preview floor and private registration instructions identify documented requirements. Account admission, actual per-location state, and later-version SDK/runtime compatibility remain outside this evidence.

answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers/accept-with-connect describes private-preview Connect acceptance with Stripe version 2026-05-27.preview or later and a location plus capability request on behalf of the merchant of record (new raw lines 9-42). The related API setup guide distinguishes a pending request from an active per-location capability (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:96-112,137-172,192-198`). Direct charges use the connected account's Stripe-Account header with EUR, PaymentLocation ID and conditional voucher enablement. Platform charges create the PaymentIntent on the platform, omit transfer_data, application_fee_amount and transfer_group, and the examples retain on_behalf_of for the connected account (new raw lines 46-68 and new raw lines 112-185). A saved card can be identified from PaymentMethod benefits after SetupIntent setup, or before creating the PaymentIntent from the ConfirmationToken's preview after collecting with the Payment Element (new raw lines 70-109). Detection, Intent creation and capture are distinct from issuer settlement. A post-capture connected-account balance debit can collect the platform application fee, and issuers settle voucher proceeds outside Stripe with the connected account (new raw lines 187-235). The May guide used a provisioned SIRET directly and otherwise had the same charge-type matrix and direction of fees and settlement (old raw lines 12-50 and old raw lines 163-218). source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-connect.md preserves those established boundaries but still reads as the May request contract and omits the preview floor and activation boundary.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers/accept-with-connect, the substantive change is the preview-versioned move from entering a literal provisioned SIRET in the Connect PaymentIntent to locating the merchant-of-record branch and requesting its capability, then passing the location and conditional benefit (old raw lines 25-50 and old raw lines 112-160, new raw lines 38-59 and new raw lines 130-185). The separate November payment guide resolves SIRET at confirmation, which matters if the location changes after creation. The November overview still describes literal provisioning and the Dashboard setup guide is a separate onboarding UI that exposes a Payment Location ID (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md:58-74`, `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-2026-11-07.md:119-129`, `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-2026-11-07.md:38-56`). source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-connect.md and the reciprocal voucher concept and setup/overview routes should date the two request shapes. The setup API's destination-charge example illustrates merchant-of-record provisioning and the Connect payment matrix still prohibits destination and separate charges and transfers (new raw lines 25-36 and new raw lines 112-183; `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:312-340`). The old scalar and new array in PaymentMethod benefits conflict with the November overview's scalar and with the Connect ConfirmationToken example's still-scalar shape. Keep the object paths and example uncertainty explicit (old raw lines 58-92 and new raw lines 74-109; `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-2026-11-07.md:131-148`). Waitlist instructions provide a preview access request path. Table styling, Node-to-cURL fee examples and the diagram preserve the earlier routing and settlement behavior (old raw lines 163-218 and new raw lines 187-235). The platform fee transfer remains conditional on Account Debits requirements (`raw/stripe-connect-account-debits-2026-11-07.md:15-56`). Its reversal concerns the application fee. The captures establish documented conditions and examples without establishing preview admission, voucher payment, balance availability or settlement for a specific transaction.
